lesson.title: Check what a standard actually proves
lesson.summary: Check the legal citation and the requirements it actually covers.

blocks: A **harmonised standard** is a technical standard developed through the Union standardisation framework. Standards are generally voluntary. Article 40 gives a presumption of conformity where the relevant reference is published in the **Official Journal**, the Union's official publication, and the system conforms to the standard or applicable parts.

sources.title: Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act

blocks: A **limited presumption** concerns only requirements covered by that standard or part. A standard's title, publication by a standards body, or development work does not establish the necessary Official Journal reference. Check the exact identifier, edition, citation, restrictions and coverage before relying on the presumption.

sources.title: Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act

blocks: Keep a citation record and a requirement-by-requirement coverage map. The Commission's standardisation request must address coherence, sector frameworks and relevant technical requirements. Article 40(3) concerns participation in standards development; it does not turn every international standard into a harmonised AI Act standard.

sources.title: Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act

blocks: Fictional **Standard S** has a stipulated Official Journal citation covering one logging requirement, with a stated restriction. This is an exercise, not a real cited standard. Its coverage does not establish conformity of Northbridge's oversight or data practices. For an actual release, look up the current citation rather than assuming this toy standard exists.

sources.title: Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act
